subject.title: Feature: TTS delivery mode option — separate text + voice messages on Telegram

question: Should OpenClaw add a public Telegram TTS delivery policy for separate text-plus-voice delivery, and should that policy live under global `messages.tts`, Telegram/channel config, or a channel capability contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public configuration and overlaps with captioned-final, voice-only, and Feishu preserve-text directions, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Approve a narrow delivery policy
options.body: Define a backward-compatible mode such as `captioned`/`bundled` versus `separate`, document it, and require Telegram unit plus live proof before implementation.

options.title: Standardize captioned delivery
options.body: Keep Telegram voice captions as the supported default and document tagged/manual splitting plus overflow fallback instead of adding a new mode now.

options.title: Defer until captioned-final settles
options.body: Wait for the captioned-final TTS PR direction before deciding whether separate delivery should be first-class.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow delivery policy
recommendation.body: Define a backward-compatible mode such as `captioned`/`bundled` versus `separate`, document it, and require Telegram unit plus live proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across core TTS policy, Telegram caption delivery, and public config boundaries involved in this decision.
